provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Mech family batch. Insurance-driven and franchise-heavy, so copy leans on the independent, locally owned angle. Never promises claim outcomes, coverage or drying times, never gives insurance or legal advice, makes no mold health claims and names no equipment or franchise brands.

pageStructurePlus.section: The first 48 hours after water damage
pageStructurePlus.contains: Water extraction, moisture mapping, drying equipment placement, daily moisture readings, when wet drywall and carpet pad come out, and what the homeowner should and shouldn't touch
pageStructurePlus.why: A flooded homeowner is in shock and wants to know what happens next. A clear first-days page makes the restoration company feel in control before the truck arrives.

pageStructurePlus.section: Your insurance claim, step by step
pageStructurePlus.contains: What to photograph first, how the adjuster visit works, the moisture logs and photo documentation the restorer provides, and bracketed notes the owner confirms, with no promise of coverage
pageStructurePlus.why: Every restoration job runs through an insurer. Homeowners choose the company that explains the claim process plainly without promising what the policy will pay.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Emergency board-up and roof tarp, soot and smoke residue cleaning, odour treatment, contents cleaning, and when rebuild starts
pageStructurePlus.why: Fire customers face a long road and many strangers in the house. Mapping each stage of fire restoration earns their trust for the whole job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Containment, removal of affected materials, air filtration, cleaning, independent clearance testing where required, and preventing the moisture that caused it, with no health claims
pageStructurePlus.why: Mold buyers are anxious and suspicious of upsells. Showing a disciplined remediation process is what separates a pro from a bleach-and-paint crew.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Room-by-room inventory with photos, cleaning of salvageable contents, secure storage, the non-salvageable list for the claim, and return when the house is ready
pageStructurePlus.why: People worry about their belongings as much as the house. A pack-out page shows the restoration company treats both with care.

designDirections.name: Local Response
designDirections.bestFor: Owner-run water damage and mitigation crews with one or two trucks competing against franchise territories
designDirections.headlineSample: Water damage cleanup in {City}, from a locally owned crew
designDirections.whyItFits: Cobalt on white and a plain grotesque read like clean water and a clear plan, with the local owner's name above everything a franchise page can't say.

designDirections.name: Flood and Fire Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Restoration companies running water, fire and mold jobs with an on-call crew and insurance documentation
designDirections.headlineSample: Water or fire damage in {City}? Call the local restoration crew
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. A red call button and mono labels for hours, service area and moisture readings read like a job log, the calm order a flooded family needs.

designDirections.name: Claim to Rebuild
designDirections.bestFor: Full-service restoration contractors that carry jobs from mitigation through the insurance claim to the finished rebuild
designDirections.headlineSample: From first call to final rebuild, restoration in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen and a classical serif feel like an insurer's letter, which suits a long, paperwork-heavy restoration where trust matters more than speed.

openers.line: {Business Name} looks like a locally owned restoration crew on the map, but there's no website. When a basement floods, the franchise pages are all anyone finds.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A restoration site that says you're local and owner-run: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Facebook in place of a site
openers.line: Your listing goes to Facebook. Someone standing in an inch of water wants to know what happens in the next few hours, not scroll through drying equipment posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest water or fire damage job.
openers.linkLine: A water damage page made for that moment: {demo-link}

openers.line: The restoration site on your profile has an old year in the footer and a broken contact form. On the worst day of someone's year, that's enough to make them call a franchise instead.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for an old year, a host banner or a dead form. Note which you found.
openers.linkLine: Same restoration company, current and calm on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your water damage page loads slowly on my phone and the number isn't tappable. People calling about a burst pipe are on a phone with wet hands.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note load time and the call button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your restoration site rebuilt for a phone in a flooded room: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online tells a homeowner what your crew does in the first day after water damage. That's the question they ask on every call, and a page would answer it at 2 a.m.
openers.hook: Check whether any page or post explains the mitigation steps. If not, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A first 48 hours water damage page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most of your restoration jobs go through an insurance claim, and homeowners have no idea how that works. A plain page on the claim steps makes you the calm one in the room.
openers.hook: Look for posts or reviews mentioning insurance or adjusters. Quote one if you find it.
openers.linkLine: An insurance claim steps page for restoration: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Reviews about calm in a crisis
openers.line: Your reviews talk about a crew that kept a family calm while the basement was pumped out. That's the restoration story that wins the next call, and it lives only on the map.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one specific phrase about a flood, fire or mold job. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those restoration reviews next to the water damage page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first deep freeze and the spring storms bring burst pipes and flooded basements all over {City}. The local restoration crew that's easy to find that week stays busy all season.
openers.hook: Use this before winter or the spring storm season. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the burst-pipe and storm calls: {demo-link}

openers.line: Water heaters and supply lines burst overnight. If your restoration line rolls to a full mailbox, that homeowner calls the national number on the franchise ad instead.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A water damage request that works overnight: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring restoration technicians. Good techs compare a local outfit with the franchises, and a site that shows your crew and your jobs helps them choose you.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or story. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A restoration company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing doesn't say your restoration trucks reach {Neighborhood}. Franchise maps claim every town, so a true list of where your crew goes is worth more than it looks.
openers.hook: Find towns named in reviews or posts. Use the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: A restoration page for each town your crew covers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Some of your posts show mold remediation behind old leaks. Mold buyers are wary of upsells, and a page showing your containment and clearance process wins their trust.
openers.hook: Only if they post mold work. Note one job you saw.
openers.linkLine: A mold remediation process page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

openers.line: If your crew holds restoration training certificates, nobody can see them from your listing. Putting certifications and insurance on a page is how a local company stands next to a franchise.
openers.hook: Look for certificate logos or mentions on their profile. Never claim a credential they haven't shown.
openers.linkLine: Certifications and insurance on one restoration page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your restoration work comes from plumbers and insurance agents. If one of them signs with a franchise programme, that work stops overnight.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts mentioning a plumber or agent referral. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where your restoration referrals could land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows careful restoration work, containment up and drying equipment set right. A stranger should see that before they see a franchise logo.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted job and name it exactly: water, fire or mold, and the room.
openers.linkLine: That restoration job, front and centre: {demo-link}

Want to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried under drying jobs. Sample restoration site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a first 48 hours water damage page, a plain insurance claim walkthrough that promises nothing about coverage, and fire, mold and pack-out pages, all leading with the fact that you're local. If it's not for you, say so and I'll stop.

IF YES:
"What did you make of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"It's not a lead programme and there's no referral fee. It's a site you own. The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many service and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your company I'd say about {Build Price}, a small part of one water job."
"Ten minutes this week to walk through it?"

CLOSE:

objections.objection: All my work comes from insurance agents and plumbers.
objections.handler: "Then the site is for them as much as homeowners. Agents and plumbers send the homeowner a link, and the claim page makes you look like the safe choice."

objections.objection: The franchises outspend me on ads. I can't compete online.
objections.handler: "You won't outspend them. You can out-local them: your name, your crew, your town list. Plenty of people search for an independent after a bad franchise experience."

objections.objection: I'm on a program with an insurance company already.
objections.handler: "Program work is valuable and it sets your rates. A site brings in jobs where the homeowner picks the restorer, which you control."

objections.objection: I can't talk about insurance online, it's a minefield.
objections.handler: "Agreed, so the page promises nothing. It explains the steps and the documents you provide, and the wording is yours to approve line by line."

objections.objection: We're slammed after every storm. I don't need more.
objections.handler: "Then the site is for the quiet months. Mold, fire and contents work keep crews busy between storms."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}, because it's a water damage page, the claim walkthrough and fire and mold pages. One mitigation job covers it."

{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} restoration demo down Friday.

Hi {Owner}, freeze season is close and burst pipes come with it. Thought of you.

The restoration site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a small part of one mitigation job. Restoration owners think in jobs and claims, not pages.
The first 48 hours page and the claim walkthrough are the core; price them as their own lines.
Quote water, fire, mold and contents pages separately. Each is a different crisis and buyer.
Never publish coverage, drying-time or certification claims the owner hasn't approved in writing.
Referral-partner pages for plumbers and agents are worth more here than town pages.
Franchise-territory owners can't buy a separate site; qualify for independents first.

lineItems.description: Max with a step timeline, what-not-to-touch list, moisture reading explainer and an urgent request form.
Max with a photo checklist, adjuster visit steps, a documentation sample and owner-approved bracketed wording.
Max for fire, mold or contents pages with their own process steps and finished jobs.
Max with separate paths for plumbers, insurance agents and property managers and a partner referral form.
Max when each page shows its own jobs and a local review.
Max when the water damage, claim and fire pages are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at job close-out
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the drying equipment leaves and the moisture readings are dry, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review. Restoration reviews about calm and care beat any franchise ad."

whatElseYouSell.name: Licence-checked ads for water damage
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Water damage searches are the priciest clicks in the trade. I run the licence-checked local ads tightly to {City} so you pay for real floods, not job seekers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once reviews are flowing and documents are current.

whatElseYouSell.name: Plumber and agent referral kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A leave-behind card and a partner page for plumbers, insurance agents and property managers, so every flooded house they see gets your restoration number."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the referral partner page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for restoration
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each water, fire and mold job posted with the town named, and the profile kept consistent with the site, so the local crew shows up next to the franchises."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck and trailer lettering artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A restoration truck sits outside a house for days. Lettering that says locally owned, with the site and number, makes the neighbours remember who to call."

whatElseYouSell.name: Freeze-warning mailer to older neighbourhoods
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before the first freeze, older streets get a postcard on protecting pipes and what to do if one bursts, with the restoration number on the fridge side."

whatElseYouSell.name: Commercial property manager outreach
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A page and letter for commercial property managers offering a pre-loss plan, so the restoration crew is already on file when a sprinkler line bursts."

withoutAI.route: Plumbers who find the leak first
withoutAI.whoPays: The plumbing company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plumber who fixes the burst pipe before your crew dries the house needs a site too. Your water damage page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Plumbers and restoration crews hand each other every flood job.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agents who refer your restoration crew need a page for clients after a loss, explaining who to call first. You're on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents want to help clients after a loss, and the restoration owner already knows them.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Whoever rebuilds after your crew finishes mitigation needs a project site. Your introduction gets me in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Mitigation-only firms hand off rebuilds and the two trades refer constantly.

withoutAI.route: Public adjusters on water and fire losses
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The public adjusters you meet on fire losses need a site that explains their role plainly. You know which ones are good."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Adjusters live on referrals from restoration crews.

withoutAI.whoPays: The contents cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "If you sub out contents cleaning or storage, that partner needs a site, and your pack-out page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Contents firms depend on restoration referrals.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Managers whose units flood from upstairs leaks need a resident incident page. Water emergencies route to your restoration crew."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Multi-unit water losses are frequent and managers want one trusted crew.

withAI.route: Loss summary drafts for insurance agents
withAI.pitchLine: "After a client's loss, an assistant drafts a plain summary of next steps for the agent to send, with the restoration crew's number included."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want to look responsive after a loss, and the restoration client is the first call.

withAI.route: Photo inventory sorter for public adjusters
withAI.pitchLine: "Adjusters get hundreds of fire and water damage shots per loss. An assistant sorts them by room and item and drafts the photo log."
withAI.whyItWorks: Photo logs eat adjusters' evenings, and the restoration owner's introduction carries trust.

withAI.pitchLine: "From the mitigation crew's tear-out notes, an assistant drafts the rebuild scope for the contractor to price and check."
withAI.whyItWorks: It speeds the hand-off both trades depend on.

withAI.route: Leak report triage for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report water from the ceiling at night. An assistant tells them how to shut off the unit valve, flags real floods and calls the restoration crew."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers cut damage and dispatch time, and the restoration client gets the jobs.

withAI.pitchLine: "The plumber who sends you water damage jobs loses repair quotes to slow callbacks. Follow-up texts set up for them in a week."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's configuration, and the introduction comes from a trusted partner.

withAI.route: Contents inventory helper for pack-out partners
withAI.pitchLine: "Photograph each box at pack-out and an assistant drafts the item list by room for the claim, for the crew to check."
withAI.whyItWorks: Contents inventories are tedious and claim-critical, and both firms gain.

softwareAI.name: Flood call text-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed restoration call gets a text asking whether the water is still running and whether the main is off, so the crew calls the active flood first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Moisture reading log app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Techs log daily moisture readings by room and point on a phone, and the drying log for the claim builds itself."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current drying log format and the meters they use.

softwareAI.name: Restoration review reply drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a reply drafted in the owner's voice that mentions the water, fire or mold job, without any claim or policy details."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests running. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job photo documentation by room
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every water damage shot tagged by room, date and stage, so the claim package is organised before the adjuster asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their documentation checklist.

softwareAI.name: Overnight water damage answering line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers flood calls overnight, walks the caller through shutting off the water and power safety, takes photos and dispatches the on-call restoration crew."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before freeze season. Needs on-call rules and safety wording they approve. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Drying log narrative writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the daily moisture readings and tech notes, it drafts the job narrative the adjuster expects, for the owner to check before it goes out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a few past job files. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the owner reviews every word.

softwareAI.name: Equipment tracker by job
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every dehumidifier, air mover and scrubber tracked by job and day, so nothing is forgotten at a finished house and every day is billed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their equipment list.

softwareAI.name: Homeowner job portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner sees the drying progress, the next visit and the documents sent to their insurer, and stops calling the office for updates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the moisture log and photo documentation in place first.

softwareAI.name: Contents inventory by photo
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Photograph each room's belongings at pack-out and it drafts the itemised contents list for the claim, for the crew to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a few past inventories. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Q&A assistant for restoration customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how long will the fans run' and 'what does the adjuster need' from the owner's own notes, and never says what a policy covers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Referral partner tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every plumber, agent and manager who refers restoration work, with jobs sent and thank-yous due, so no partner goes quiet unnoticed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their referral list.

softwareAI.name: Job status texts to homeowners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each stage, extraction done, drying in progress, ready for rebuild, sends the homeowner a text automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their job stages.

softwareAI.name: Restoration dispatch board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New losses, daily drying checks and pack-outs on one board by crew and truck, so a storm week doesn't run off three phones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, at three or more crews.

softwareAI.name: Estimate line drafting from scope notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the walkthrough notes, it drafts the mitigation estimate lines on the owner's template, for the estimator to check and adjust."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past estimates and their template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Receivables chaser for insurance-paid jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Unpaid restoration invoices trigger polite reminders to the homeowner and the right contact on schedule, so jobs don't sit unpaid for months."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their open invoices and reminder wording.

softwareAI.name: Mold job clearance tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every mold remediation job with containment dates, removal, cleaning and the independent clearance result, in one record."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, for firms doing mold work.

softwareAI.name: Freeze alert to past customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a hard freeze is forecast for {City}, past customers get a text on protecting pipes and the restoration number if one bursts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs the customer list and a weather feed.

softwareAI.name: Profit by loss type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether water, fire, mold or contents jobs make the company money once equipment days, labour and slow payments are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of jobs and payments.

softwareAI.name: Technician training library
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The lead tech explains drying set-ups and containment on a phone, and it becomes a restoration how-to library for new hires."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Restoration tech applicant screen
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they can take night flood calls, handle heavy equipment and work in fire-damaged homes, before anyone calls them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the moisture log for independents
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Independent restorers compete with franchises that have corporate software. A simple moisture log and documentation app levels that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Independents need claim-ready documentation and can't afford enterprise tools.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member restoration companies a locally owned site template with a first 48 hours page and claim walkthrough."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations of independents want to help members compete with franchises.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Equipment rental and supply dealer locator
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A locator of independent restoration firms who buy drying equipment from you, so homeowners find a local crew."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want independent customers to survive franchise competition.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every agency in your network needs an after-loss page for clients. I've written the restoration side already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agency networks share marketing budgets and need content clients actually use.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "License my restoration template with the first 48 hours page and a compliant claim walkthrough already written."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Claim wording is risky to write from scratch, so agencies pay for a vetted version.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A pre-loss plan page per building with shut-off locations, contacts and the restoration crew on call."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers want a plan before the sprinkler bursts, and the restoration client is on it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "After a flood, residents need plain steps on drying out safely and checking contractors. A public page answers it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Emergency offices have outreach budgets and need practical recovery content.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Plumbing companies across the region want a trusted restoration partner page for flooded customers. Build once, sell to each."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Plumbers face water damage weekly and want a clean hand-off.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Storm-season kit for restorers in other metros
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Restoration companies outside your metro, monthly
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A switch-on storm banner, freeze alert text and flood page any independent restorer can turn on the week weather hits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every restorer needs it at once, so it sells as a kit.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A portal that carries each restoration job from mitigation to rebuild with the homeowner, the adjuster and the crew in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Full-service restorers lose jobs at the hand-off and pay to fix it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A restoration company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one independent restoration crew per metro. {City}'s is signed; the next city's best locally owned restorer is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Independents value exclusivity against franchises, and the demo carries over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Mold assessor and testing company sites
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Independent mold assessors who run clearance testing need sites that explain their role separate from remediation."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Assessors depend on restorers for referrals and rarely have good sites.

upsellLadder.offer: Restoration site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Your restoration site and care plan on one contract, so a storm banner or new crew shot is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first water damage job booked through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "That family's basement is dry. Let's ask every restoration customer for a review when the fans leave."

upsellLadder.trigger: A plumber or agent sends a job through the partner page.
upsellLadder.line: "A plumber just referred through the site. Let's put a restoration card in every partner's truck."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention an adjuster asking for drying logs again.
upsellLadder.line: "The adjuster wants drying logs again. Let's have the techs build them on the phone."

upsellLadder.trigger: A freeze or storm brings overnight calls that went to voicemail.
upsellLadder.line: "Those overnight water damage calls went to a franchise. This answers them and dispatches your restoration crew."

upsellLadder.trigger: Steady new reviews and current licence and insurance documents.
upsellLadder.line: "Your restoration reviews are strong enough for the licence-checked ads. Let's catch the next freeze's searches."

upsellLadder.trigger: They add a third crew or run several losses after one storm.
upsellLadder.line: "Three crews and a storm week need one restoration board. Let's build it before the next one."
